# Geodrome

> Interactive 3D Geodesics & Diametric Antipodes Engine

Geodrome is a modernized, open-source 3D WebGL spherical visualizer and 2D Mercator map projection engine designed to explore Great Circle navigation, orthodromic paths, and diametric antipodal geometry. Inspired by science communicator Ralph Crewe.

## Primary Resources

- [Geodrome Production Engine](https://geodrome.pages.dev): Live WebGL interactive 3D globe and 2D Mercator map visualizer.
- [About & Engineering Story](https://geodrome.pages.dev/about): Technical breakdown, origin story, and geodesic mathematical principles.
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/ny-collins/geodrome): Open-source TypeScript codebase, build scripts, and issue tracker.
- [Developer Guidelines](https://github.com/ny-collins/geodrome/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPMENT_GUIDELINES.md): Architectural principles, coding conventions, VRAM lifecycle, and mathematical projection models.

## Core Features

- Interactive 3D WebGL Globe: Orbit controls, camera interpolation, double-tap raycasting coordinate lookup.
- Dual Projection Sync: Synchronized 3D WebGL sphere and 2D Mercator canvas with seam-clipping date line math.
- Geodesic Pathfinding: 3-second animated geodesic tube growth along 8 compass bearings.
- Antipodal Mathematics: Diametric opposite point computation with internal core diameter tunnel lines.
- Dual-Pass X-Ray Transparency: Two-pass THREE.BackSide hollow sphere rendering.

## Mathematical Specifications

- 3D Spherical UV Coordinates: X = r * sin(phi) * cos(theta), Y = r * cos(phi), Z = -r * sin(phi) * sin(theta) where phi = (90 - lat) * rad and theta = lng * rad.
- 2D Mercator Projection: lngToX(lng) = (((lng + 180) % 360 + 360) % 360) / 360 * width.
